what_it_does: When engineers design or stress-test storage systems (hard drives, SSDs, storage arrays), they need realistic recordings of how data is read and written over time — called I/O traces — to benchmark their designs. Generating fake but realistic traces is hard because real storage workloads involve multiple devices that interact with each other in complex, time-varying ways that older synthetic tools fail to reproduce faithfully. DiTTO applies diffusion models — the same family of AI models used to generate images by gradually refining random noise into a coherent picture — to instead generate sequences of storage I/O events that mimic the statistical patterns and inter-device dependencies of real traces. The system lets users configure the characteristics they want (e.g., workload intensity, number of devices), and the paper claims only an 8% error rate in matching the requested configuration. Based only on the abstract, this is described as a late-breaking result, meaning it is a preliminary finding rather than a fully developed and evaluated system.
